claims.text: Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 produces amorphous fractions only under very fast cooling.
Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 exhibits a complex, multi-step crystallization response during heating.
Approximately 3–5 at.% B should be introduced by substituting an unspecified fraction of the base elements.
Adding 3–5 at.% B will enhance glass-forming ability during rapid quenching.
Adding 3–5 at.% B will improve thermal stability during subsequent reheating.
Cooling rates above 10^6 K/s will form an amorphous phase in the proposed alloy.
B addition will enhance chemical short-range order in the amorphous matrix.
B addition will produce denser atomic packing in the amorphous matrix.
B is an efficient network former in this alloy context.
B will form additional bonds and local network structures that lower atomic mobility.
The reduced atomic mobility will retard crystalline-phase nucleation during solidification.
The reduced atomic mobility will retard crystalline-phase nucleation during thermal analysis.
The B-modified alloy will retain amorphous material over a broader range of cooling rates than the unmodified alloy.
The B-modified alloy will exhibit a single, sharper crystallization event during reheating.
The B-modified alloy will have a higher crystallization-onset temperature than Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
B concentrations above approximately 5 at.% may cause phase separation.
B concentrations above approximately 5 at.% may cause brittleness.
Lower cooling rates may fail to produce the desired amorphous phase.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies substitution of base elements with 3–5 at.% B, whereas the experiment describes a batch with an 'additional' 3–5 at.% B. These imply different normalized compositions.
